title: Two sections of a line bundle glued from reciprocal functions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U,V$ opens covering $X$, and $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, $g\in\mathcal O_X(V)$ such that their restrictions to $U\cap V$ multiply to $1$ and $D(g)=U\cap V$ (the basic open where the germ of $g$ is a unit). There exist an invertible module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and two compatible global sections $s,t$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] such that $X_s=U$ and $V\subseteq X_t$, with nonvanishing loci as in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No integral, separated, Noetherian, dimension, affine, or finiteness hypotheses are required.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NB (varieties-lemma-find-globally-generated), proof, cocycle, two sections, and locus calculation

proof.text: On U intersect V, g is a unit with inverse f. Use g as the frame transition e_U = g e_V, inverse on the reversed overlap, and identity on the equal-index overlaps. The Cech identities follow by cancellation. Glue to an invertible module L and free frames e_U,e_V using the transition-cocycle theorem.

The local pairs (e_U,g e_V) and (f e_U,e_V) agree on the overlap because e_U = g e_V and fg = 1. The sheaf axiom glues them to global s,t. Restriction to every open gives compatible sections s,t in L.sections.

A free local frame identifies the stalk with its local ring and the maximal-ideal multiple of the stalk with the maximal ideal. Therefore a section c e is nonvanishing at x precisely when the germ of c is a unit. On U, s=e_U is nonvanishing; on V, s=g e_V has locus D(g)=U intersect V. The cover yields X_s=U. On V, t=e_V is nonvanishing, so V is contained in X_t. Empty charts are harmless.

lean.statement: theorem exists_line_bundle_sections_of_reciprocal_cover (X : Scheme.{u}) (U V : X.Opens) (f : Γ(X, U)) (g : Γ(X, V)) (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤) (hinv : X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op f * X.presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op g = 1) (hlocus : X.basicOpen g = U ⊓ V) : ∃ (L : X.Modules) (s t : L.sections), L.IsInvertible ∧ nonvanishingLocus L (s.val (Opposite.op ⊤)) = (U : Set X) ∧ (V : Set X) ⊆ nonvanishingLocus L (t.val (Opposite.op ⊤))
